destination.name: Bathurst
destination.tagline: Australia's oldest inland settlement, known for a motor-racing circuit that is a public road outside race weeks.
destination.description: Bathurst is a city of 44,621 people (2023) on the Central Tablelands, about 200 km west-north-west of Sydney, founded in 1815 as the oldest inland settlement in Australia. It was the site of Australia's first payable gold discovery in 1851, and its centre keeps ornate gold-rush buildings. Most visitors come for Mount Panorama, the circuit that hosts the Bathurst 1000 each October and the Bathurst 12 Hour each February, and is open to ordinary traffic the rest of the time. Two museums, one on motor racing and one on fossils and minerals, are the other main stops.
whyVisit: Explore the National Motor Racing Museum
See fossils at the Fossil and Mineral Museum

goodToKnow.title: Race weeks
goodToKnow.detail: Mount Panorama is open to public traffic only outside race periods; the Bathurst 1000 is each October and the population swells with tourists.

goodToKnow.title: Museum prices
goodToKnow.detail: The National Motor Racing Museum and the Australian Fossil and Mineral Museum each charge about $15 and open 9 AM to 4:30 PM.

goodToKnow.title: Other race events
goodToKnow.detail: The Bathurst 12 Hour (each February) and the Bathurst Motor Festival (each Easter) also swell the population, so book ahead for those dates.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} give mild, settled weather for the circuit drive and museums, with autumn and spring between warm summers and cool to cold winters.
